title: India Boosts 'Make in India' Electronics: What the PLI Scheme Means for You
description: The government is giving financial incentives to companies that make more electronics in India. This is part of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, .

faq.a: PLI stands for "Production Linked Incentive." It's a scheme where the government gives financial rewards linked to how much a company produces and sells.

faq.q: Which sectors are currently covered by PLI schemes?
faq.a: Currently, PLI schemes cover 14 key sectors, including large-scale electronics manufacturing, IT hardware, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, telecom products, white goods (ACs, LEDs), solar PV modules, textiles, and more.

faq.q: How long do companies receive incentives under PLI?
faq.a: Typically, incentives are provided for a period of 5 to 6 years, following a base year for calculation.

The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) is the main coordinating body. However, individual schemes are implemented and monitored by their respective ministries, such as the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) for electronics.

faq.q: What are the main goals of the PLI scheme?
faq.a: The primary goals are to boost domestic manufacturing, attract investments (both local and foreign), increase exports, create employment, and make Indian industries more competitive globally.
